rationale: Initial baseline used swizzle=[0], block_M=32 (only divisor of M=32), block_N=64, block_K=32, 3 stages, 18432 B smem, 78 regs, 147.7 us simulated, 33.8 MB DRAM, 5 blocks/SM. Since M=32, reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(32/32))=1 for any swizzle value, so the panel-reuse hypothesis cannot reduce traffic on this skinny-M workload; nevertheless we broaden swizzle to [0,4,8,16] per protocol and to test whether serpentine ordering affects the simulator at all. block_M fixed at 32 (divisibility). block_N [64,128] and block_K [32,64] retained; stages [1,2,3] retained. All choices still fit the 32768-byte cap (worst case block_N=128, block_K=64 requires stages<=2 due to 2*64*(32+128)*stages; solver enforces this). Weights left equal because traffic is already dominated by the block_N term (reuse=1) and footprint has headroom; next hypothesis: test whether larger block_N/block_K with lower stages, and non-zero swizzle, lower simulated latency and DRAM through better coalescing, without exceeding the portability cap. Metal results validate numerics for the exact source/config/TIR but do not execute CUDA binaries; GB10 values are simulator estimates only.
